extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, regulators, automakers, and the public
extracted.subtask_description: Transcript of a congressional oversight hearing focused on EPA/CARB testing, enforcement, and remedies related to Volkswagen defeat devices and excess vehicle emissions. Covers testing protocols, enforcement options, mitigation, consumer impacts, and information-sharing expectations of manufacturers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust compliance and oversight testing
rubrics_metrics.description: What is required for a robust compliance and oversight program is both testing of new vehicles in the lab, testing of what we call in-use vehicles in the lab as on-road measurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testing must include laboratory testing of new models and testing of in-use vehicles with on-road measurements; testing programs should be unpredictable to avoid evasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpredictability of testing
rubrics_metrics.description: The bottom line, madam, is that we are going to be unpredictable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reveal specific new testing procedures to automakers. Keep methods confidential so manufacturers cannot design software to recognize test conditions and cheat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of laboratory cycles, off-cycle dyno testing, and real-world monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: It will be a combination of both these five cycles that we test on today, what we call off-cycle dyno testing as well as this real-world onboard monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple prescribed test cycles, off-cycle dynamometer tests, and mobile/on-road devices to capture real-world emissions profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturer testing and EPA audit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: We require the manufacturers to test every new model of vehicle and submit that data to us, which we review along with design. We audit a certain percentage of those by testing them in our laboratory on prescribed test cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturers must perform and submit model-level certification testing; regulators should select and audit a subset via independent lab testing and on-road verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on tailpipe emissions outcome rather than source code parsing
rubrics_metrics.description: We don't need to unpack 100 million lines of code to find these defeat devices. The bottom line is testing them in unpredictable ways... what's coming out of the tailpipe and does it meet our standard?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory evaluation should prioritize measurable emissions results (tailpipe output) activated in diverse conditions over exhaustive code review, although code may inform investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority testing population
rubrics_metrics.description: Our first priority is to test all light-duty diesel vehicles. We're starting with diesels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize testing by technology and risk profile (e.g., light-duty diesels first), then expand scope based on findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of interagency and international partnerships in testing
rubrics_metrics.description: We have teamed up with California and Environment Canada, both who have the capabilities, as we do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with state, national, and international partners to leverage technical capacity and data comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and documentation requests from manufacturers
rubrics_metrics.description: We were informed that the vehicles had a dual-calibration strategy... Has VW provided EPA with an engine map that shows specifically how the defeat device works for each model car... They have outstanding official document requests, and we will be promulgating more of those.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulators should request detailed technical documentation (engine maps, calibration details) and internal investigation records from manufacturers; lack of cooperation should be recorded and followed up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy evaluation centered on consumer and environmental impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: We are going to take a very careful look at what impact this is going to have on owners and consumers. That will be central to how we review the options that Volkswagen comes forward to. The most important thing going forward is that those defeat devices are removed, that these vehicles are addressed in a way that will work for consumers and the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating proposed fixes/remedies regulators must assess consumer impacts (e.g., trunk space, usability) alongside environmental effectiveness; fixes must both remove defeat functionality and be practical for owners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation as part of settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: We're looking for the opportunities, the ways in which the damage that has been done to the environment... can be addressed. Many of our settlements look forward and ask the question, how is it that we can make air quality better than what the law minimally requires in any given instance? That additional reduction in pollution is what we refer to as mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement settlements should include mitigation projects that yield additional emissions reductions (e.g., third-party wood stove changeout programs) to address environmental and public health harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of penalty funds toward remediation or reward
rubrics_metrics.description: Would it be helpful... to allow a portion of the fine money in a fraud case like this to go to the university that discovered it?... we take some of their ill-gained goods... and the government gives it back to some of the folks who helped discover it, law enforcement and prosecutors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider legislative or settlement mechanisms to allocate penalty funds for mitigation projects or to reward independent discoverers (e.g., universities/NGOs) that uncover violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and scope of enforcement (civil, criminal, corporate, individual)
rubrics_metrics.description: I can't speculate now as to exactly what course all the enforcement actions will take... we're working with the Department of Justice on these matters... Certainly it is a possibility [of criminal action]. I will assure you that I am aware of absolutely no provision of the Clean Air Act which would allow a prosecution for the things that you are talking about [against individual owners].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should determine who (individuals, groups, corporate entities) is responsible; enforcement may include civil penalties, mitigation obligations, and potentially criminal charges depending on findings and applicable law; regulators should coordinate with DOJ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer protection and repair responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: These cars are safe to drive. They will not be held responsible for any repairs. That would be the responsibility of the company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory remedies should ensure consumers are not financially responsible for required repairs or fixes; companies bear repair liabilities for noncompliant vehicles.

rubrics_metrics.name: State registration and inspection interplay with federal enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you live in an area that does regular emissions tests... some states require that, in order to re-register the vehicle, if it is subject to a recall, to show that the fix has been made. Other states do not have that requirement. It depends on where you're living.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumer outcomes (e.g., penalties, registration restrictions) depend on state-level inspection and recall enforcement; federal actions should consider these state-level regulatory interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information transparency to oversight bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you asked them whether or not they would share that information with EPA?... They have not agreed at this time. We have outstanding official document requests, and we will be promulgating more of those. Yes, we will [let the committee know if VW does not provide the results].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should pursue document production and commit to informing congressional oversight and other stakeholders about compliance with information requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resourcing for real-world testing
rubrics_metrics.description: The easiest solution is to give EPA more resources, so it can perform the real-world testing... you don't want to rely on the happenstance investigation of a small NGO to trigger one of the largest global recalls around.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in agency capacity (funding, personnel, mobile monitoring equipment) to perform systematic real-world emissions testing rather than relying solely on external actors to discover cheats.
